base: Prices are for a pool up to about 16 x 32 ft with clear water. The size and water factors scale them, and the member's own prices win.
minutes_basis: Minutes per visit are a judgment call, except the one-time cleaning: Thumbtack says an average-sized pool takes an hour and a half to two hours. Time your own visits and change them.

packages.label: Pool service visit
includes: Skim the surface and brush walls and steps
Test the water and add routine chemicals
packages.basis: Fixr and Home Gnome: weekly maintenance $20 to $50 a visit. Home Gnome: plans of $100 to $320 a month, about $25 to $80 a visit, its own average $38. Routine chemicals in the visit price is a judgment call from the Thumbtack examples, which all include chemicals. If you bill chemicals on their own, check current rates.

sources.says: A pool owner can expect to pay $20 to $50 per week on an annual contract with weekly visits; weekly maintenance typically involves checking pH levels, cleaning the filters, putting in chemicals to avoid stains and algae, and recognizing malfunctioning equipment. Monthly pool service $30 to $90 a month.
Average pool maintenance cost by frequency: weekly $20 to $50, monthly $43 to $190, annual $808 to $2,000.

Pool cleaning plans typically range from about $100 to $320 a month; on a standard four-visit schedule that works out to roughly $25 to $80 a visit. Home Gnome: 413 completed pool care jobs, average $38 a visit. A typical weekly visit: water testing and chemical balancing, skimming, brushing walls and steps, vacuuming the floor, emptying pump and skimmer baskets, equipment inspection.

A Thumbtack pro in Phoenix charges $60 a month to only check chemicals and $90 a month for weekly full-service visits that include skimming, brushing, emptying all baskets and an equipment check. Treatments like a chlorine shock, phosphate removers, clarifiers, algaecide and backwashing are usually charged extra.

Monthly maintenance examples, all including pool chemicals: $80 (Integrity Pool Care), $85 to $120 (Humble Bee Pool Service and Repair), $90 to $95 by pool size (Radiance Pools, which emails weekly logs and photos of services performed and chemicals added). A chlorine pool uses $300 to $800 in chemicals a year, priced into pool cleaning services.

packages.label: Chemical check visit
packages.basis: Judgment call: Thumbtack's Phoenix pro charges $60 a month to only check chemicals and Humble Bee $65 to $80 a month for chemical-only service, about $14 to $19 a visit at about 4.3 weekly visits a month. The owner skims, brushes and empties the baskets.

sources.says: A Thumbtack pro in Phoenix charges $60 a month to only check chemicals and $90 a month for weekly full-service visits.

For monthly chemical-only pool service, Humble Bee charges $65 to $80, depending on the pool's size; the homeowner skims and brushes the pool and empties the skimmer baskets, and the pros handle all the chemical additions and adjustments.

packages.label: One-time pool cleaning
includes: Skim, brush and vacuum the whole pool
Test the water and add routine chemicals
packages.basis: Thumbtack: one-time cleaning outside a service contract $150 to $300 (average $225) and $148 to $413 nationally (most about $201); HomeAdvisor $116 to $357 a visit; Home Gnome $102 to $175 for a 200 sq ft pool; Fixr one-time visits $90 to $270 by pool size.

sources.says: One-time cleaning (outside of a service contract): average $225, range $150 to $300. Cleaning an average-sized pool takes an hour and a half to two hours; a larger pool three to five hours.
The national average cost to hire a pool cleaner for a one-time cleaning ranges from around $148 to $413, and most people pay around $201; one-time pool cleanings cost $229 to $278 on average.
Professional pool maintenance costs between $116 and $357 per visit, with an average of $236; labor runs $75 to $100 an hour.
The cost to maintain a 200-square-foot pool ranges between $102 and $175 for a one-time maintenance service, including cleaning, balancing chemicals and testing pH.

One-time visits that are not included in maintenance plans cost $90 to $270, depending on the size of the pool and the maintenance or cleaning needed; by size, a small 10 x 20 ft pool $60 to $285 and a large 20 x 40 ft pool $120 to $380.

packages.label: Pool opening
includes: Water topped up, cleaned and tested
packages.basis: Fixr: $250 to $350, average $300 (above-ground $175 to $225, in-ground $250 to $400); HomeAdvisor and Home Gnome $150 to $300; Thumbtack $85 to $350.

sources.says: Pool opening costs range from $250 to $350, with a national average of $300; low cost $175 for a partial opening of an above-ground pool, high cost $500 for a full opening with vacuuming and a hot tub. Above-ground $175 to $225; in-ground $250 to $400.
If you need professional help, opening your pool costs between $150 and $300, and the same goes for closing it for the winter.
Opening a pool $150 to $300: removing the cover, cleaning debris, inspecting equipment and testing water quality.
Opening a pool costs $85 to $350: a pro removes the cover, reassembles the filter system, cleans the water, tests its chemistry, refills it and turns on the pump and other equipment.

packages.label: Pool closing
includes: Pool cleaned and the water treated for winter
Water level lowered and lines cleared
Filter and equipment drained and stored
packages.basis: Fixr: $200 to $300, average $250 (above-ground $150 to $200, in-ground $200 to $400); HomeAdvisor $150 to $300; Home Gnome $250 to $475; Thumbtack $85 to $500. Thumbtack and HomeAdvisor: often two visits.

sources.says: Pool closing costs range from $200 to $300, with a national average of $250; low cost $150 to winterize an above-ground pool, high cost $400 for an in-ground pool with an adjacent hot tub. Above-ground $150 to $200; in-ground $200 to $400.

Opening and closing a pool: professionals charge between $150 and $300 for each service. A professional often performs the closing service in two or more visits, as the water must be shocked several days in advance of closing.
Closing a pool $250 to $475: lowering the water level, cleaning, vacuuming, backwashing and adding winterizing chemicals.
Closing (winterizing) a pool costs $85 to $500; because shocking the water takes a couple of days, a pro usually needs two visits to close a pool.

factors.label: Pool size
factors.basis: HomeAdvisor yearly maintenance by size: 10 x 20 ft $400 to $900 against 16 x 32 ft $700 to $1,200, about 0.7. Above-ground pools are often the small ones (HomeAdvisor), and Fixr prices above-ground openings at $175 to $225 against $250 to $400 in-ground and closings at $150 to $200 against $200 to $400, about 0.6 to 0.7. Thumbtack: a Cumming, GA pro charges $60 for an average pool and $75 for an extra-large one (1.25). The 1.1 step is a judgment call.

sources.says: Annual maintenance cost by pool size: 10 x 20 ft $400 to $900; 14 x 28 ft $600 to $1,100; 16 x 32 ft $700 to $1,200; 20 x 40 ft $1,000 and up. Above-ground pool costs are slightly lower overall, as they are often smaller.
A Thumbtack pro and pool cleaner in Cumming, Georgia, charges $60 to clean most average-sized pools and $75 for extra-large ones.
Opening an above-ground pool ranges from $175 to $225; opening an in-ground pool costs between $250 and $400.
The cost to winterize an above-ground pool averages $150 to $200; an in-ground pool averages $200 to $400.

factors.label: Water
factors.basis: Judgment call, check current rates: Thumbtack says treatments like a chlorine shock, clarifiers and algaecide are usually charged extra, and a pool that grew algae over the winter also needs a deep cleaning and algaecide; Fixr says opening a pool that has been closed for years costs at least $500. The 1.75 is ours.
factors.note: Judgment call. Check current rates where you live.

sources.says: You'll usually be charged extra for treatments like a chlorine shock, phosphate removers, clarifiers, algaecide and backwashing the filtration system.
If your pool grew algae over the winter and got dirty and green, you'll also need to pay for a deep cleaning and algaecide treatment.
Opening an unmaintained pool: if your pool has been closed for years, expect an opening to cost at least $500, more if repairs are needed.

addons.label: Filter cleaning
addons.basis: Fixr: filters $60 to $65; Thumbtack: two Arizona pros charge $80 and $100 a filter cleaning. In Florida, cleaning that needs equipment partly taken apart is licensed work, filter changes excepted (section 489.105): check your state before you open a filter.

sources.says: Pool cleaning cost by type: filters $60 to $65.

Cartridge filters need to be cleaned out at least once a year: Humble Bee Pool Service and Repair in Mesa, Arizona charges $100 for the service, and Radiance Pools in Tempe charges $80 per filter cleaning and recommends cleaning filters twice a year.

addons.label: Hot tub or spa
addons.basis: Fixr: opening a hot tub $50 to $75 and winterizing a hot tub or spa $50 to $100, on top of the pool.

sources.says: Additional opening costs: hot tub opening $50 to $75; vacuuming $50 to $75.
Additional closing costs: winterizing a hot tub or spa $50 to $100; cleaning and lowering the water level $55 to $200.

plans_basis: Thumbtack: you pay about the same for monthly service as for weekly or every-other-week service, because a pool cleaned more often takes less time; Home Gnome: weekly service is the standard for most home pools. No weekly discount, a judgment call.

plans_sources.says: You will pay about the same for monthly service as you will for weekly or bi-weekly service because the pool stays cleaner and takes less time to service with more frequent visits. Most pool service companies give better prices for a year-long contract.
Weekly service is the standard for most residential pools; some homeowners switch to bi-weekly service during cooler months or when the pool is used less often.
